summary: A compact, readable format for sending JSON data to LLMs with fewer tokens, plus a TypeScript library and CLI to convert both ways.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) is a compact encoding of the JSON data model designed for LLM input. It mixes YAML-style indentation for nested objects with CSV-style tables for lists of objects that share the same fields, so data takes fewer tokens while staying easy for a model to follow. Conversion is lossless both ways. This repo holds the TypeScript reference library and a command-line tool.
sixtySeconds.problem: JSON repeats every field name on every row, which wastes tokens when you put data in a prompt. TOON declares fields once and lists rows, cutting token use for uniform data.
whoFor: Developers putting structured data into prompts
Teams trying to lower LLM token costs
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Use it when you send arrays of similar objects to an LLM and want fewer tokens without losing structure.

overview: Install the library with npm install @toon-format/toon and call encode() on your data to get TOON text.
Use encodeLines() to stream large datasets, and decode functions to turn TOON back into JSON.
For quick conversions, run the CLI with npx @toon-format/cli, which auto-detects JSON or TOON from the file extension. Licensed MIT.

features.title: Fewer tokens
features.body: Matches JSON's retrieval accuracy with fewer tokens, per its benchmarks.

features.title: Lossless
features.body: Same data model as JSON, deterministic round-trips.

features.title: Tabular rows
features.body: Field list declared once for uniform objects.

features.title: Guardrails
features.body: [N] row counts and {fields} lists catch truncated output.

features.title: CLI
features.body: Convert files and show token savings with --stats.

strengths: Clear token savings for uniform data
Spec with ports in other languages
limitations: Deeply nested or non-uniform data can be smaller as compact JSON
Purely tabular data is smaller as CSV
Some local or quantized models may be faster with compact JSON
